solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Frees former European politician with leads to tax scandal (7)

indicatorNotes.leads to: the leads of words are their first letters

blocks.note: first letters of Tax and Scandal

annotation.surface: A disgraced former Euro-politician caught up in a tax scandal.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Frees' as the start of a news story; it is a plain verb, and 'with' just tacks the pieces together.
annotation.definitionFit: To exempt someone is to free them from an obligation.

entries.clue: Disorganised mess by a government building (7)

indicatorNotes.Disorganised: the letters are put out of order

annotation.surface: A shambles of a mess piling up beside an official building.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Disorganised mess' reads as one idea, but 'mess' is fodder and 'Disorganised' the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: An embassy is the building housing a foreign government's mission.

entries.clue: Read about odd part of body (7)

annotation.surface: An instruction to read up on some strange part of the anatomy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Read about' looks like 'study'; here 'about' shuffles READ. Rum is British slang for peculiar.
annotation.definitionFit: A generic definition: the eardrum is one small part of the body, the membrane that vibrates with sound.

entries.clue: Seafood uncooked in edges of pan (5)

indicatorNotes.in: one piece goes inside the other
indicatorNotes.edges of: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of PAN

annotation.surface: Raw seafood sitting at the edge of a frying pan.
annotation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture is exactly right, which hides that 'uncooked' is a piece of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the prawn is one of many shellfish sold as seafood.

entries.clue: Southern gallery intended to give out a formal account (9)

indicatorNotes.give out: to give out the A is to let it go

blocks.note: the Tate, London's famous art gallery
the A dropped from MEANT, leaving MENT

annotation.surface: A gallery in the south planning to issue an official statement to the press.
annotation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British art galleries. 'Give out' sounds like publishing the account; it actually removes A from MEANT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in a witness giving police their version of events in writing.

entries.clue: After return of loan, dad finally gets benefits and cheap means of travel (3,4)

indicatorNotes.return of: a return runs the word backwards
indicatorNotes.finally: puts the last piece at the end

blocks.note: a sub is a small loan, an advance on wages

annotation.surface: Once his loan is repaid, dad finally gets his benefits and cheap travel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dad finally' tempts you to take D, dad's last letter; instead 'finally' orders the pieces, with SS coming last. A sub is British slang for an advance of money.
annotation.definitionFit: A bus pass gives reduced or free bus fares, especially to pensioners.

entries.clue: Throws foreign money (5)

blocks.note: what an unbroken horse does to its rider
US slang for dollars, foreign to a British paper

annotation.walkthrough: 'Throws' in the rodeo sense: a bucking horse throws its rider.
annotation.definitionFit: A horse that bucks throws its rider; bucks is slang for US dollars.

entries.clue: Type of bar initially seen on trendy form of travel (9)

indicatorNotes.initially: 'initially' means at the start, so only the start of 'seen' is used

blocks.note: the space bar on a keyboard

annotation.surface: A new style of bar is spotted in a fashionable form of transport.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Type of bar' suggests a pub or a metal rod; the keyboard's space bar is what types.
annotation.definitionFit: A spaceship is a vehicle for space travel, loosely a form of travel.

entries.clue: Cunning code deciphered in style! (3,4)

indicatorNotes.deciphered: a code worked out, its letters rearranged

annotation.surface: A cunning code cracked with some flair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Style' reads as a flourish ('in style!') but is the definition: Art Deco is a design style.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the bold geometric look of 1920s and 30s design is one named style among many.

entries.clue: Play guitar holding a tuner initially to get level (7)

indicatorNotes.holding: one piece holds the others inside
indicatorNotes.initially: 'initially' means at the start, so only the start of 'tuner' is used

blocks.note: first letter of Tuner, placed inside

annotation.surface: A guitarist strums while using a tuner to get the strings level.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical picture points to tuning; 'level' is a layer, as of rock.
annotation.definitionFit: A stratum is a layer or level, of rock or of society.

entries.clue: Two pubs by area in Windsor, say (7)

annotation.surface: A couple of pubs in the area around Windsor, the royal town.
annotation.walkthrough: Windsor looks like the town; it is Barbara Windsor, the British actress of the Carry On films and the soap EastEnders, and 'say' marks her as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: Barbara is the first name of the actress Barbara Windsor.

entries.clue: Covers of cloth more appropriate for part of book (7)

indicatorNotes.Covers of: a word's covers are its outside letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of CLOTH

annotation.surface: Choosing a more suitable cloth cover for a book.
annotation.walkthrough: Cloth covers belong on books, so the bookbinding picture hides that 'covers' only means CLOTH's outside letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: books are divided into numbered sections of this name.

entries.clue: Street run enrages foreigners (9)

annotation.surface: A street race infuriates the visitors from abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Enrages' has the letters of ANGERS plus an E, which tempts an anagram, but it is a plain synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: Strangers are people from elsewhere, foreigners in an older sense.

entries.clue: Day before National Theatre performance (5)

blocks.note: the eve is the day before, as Christmas Eve

annotation.surface: The eve of a show at London's National Theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: The theatre setting makes 'performance' look like part of the show's description; it defines the whole answer.
annotation.definitionFit: An event is an occasion or performance put on for an audience.

entries.clue: Medieval landholders abandoning old country (5)

indicatorNotes.abandoning: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so the landholders go on without the O

blocks.note: yeomen held and farmed their own land

annotation.surface: Medieval landowners leaving their ancestral homeland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old country' reads as a phrase for homeland, but 'old' is the O to drop and 'country' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Yemen is a country at the south of the Arabian peninsula.

entries.clue: Went quickly over allocation for commentary (9)

indicatorNotes.over: turned over, so the word runs backwards

annotation.surface: Someone rushing through their allotted share of a commentary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Went quickly over' reads as skimming; 'over' reverses RAN.
annotation.definitionFit: Narration is a spoken commentary accompanying a film or story.

entries.clue: Rewarm hot wriggling wriggler (9)

indicatorNotes.wriggling: the letters squirm into a new order

annotation.surface: Heating up a squirming creature.
annotation.walkthrough: Indicator and definition share a root, so the clue tells you what the answer does while telling you to shuffle.
annotation.definitionFit: An earthworm is the classic wriggling creature.

entries.clue: Break precipitation and temperature control (9)

annotation.surface: A weather report: rain, then temperature control.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Temperature control' reads as one thing, like a thermostat; T is the temperature and 'control' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Restraint means control, of oneself or others.

entries.clue: Pronounces “H” in house like Captain Hook and Smee? (9)

blocks.note: the two pirates from Peter Pan

annotation.surface: Asking how the pirates of Peter Pan would say their aitches.
annotation.walkthrough: Hook and Smee are the pirates of J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan; the question mark marks them as examples. The definition reads as one idea: sounding the H at the start of 'house'.
annotation.definitionFit: To aspirate is to sound the breathy H, as at the start of 'house'.

entries.clue: Article on fool in large port (7)

annotation.surface: A newspaper article about a fool at a big port.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts AN above TWERP. 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece but means a grammatical article.
annotation.definitionFit: Antwerp in Belgium is one of Europe's largest ports.

entries.clue: Rope in decorator (7)

blocks.note: the nautical sense: a line tied to a small boat's bow
someone who paints and papers houses

annotation.surface: Roping in a decorator for a job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rope in' reads as 'recruit'; 'in' only links two meanings. The nautical painter is a mooring line.
annotation.definitionFit: A painter is both a boat's mooring rope and a house decorator.

entries.clue: Flatten papers (5)

blocks.note: as with an iron or a flower

annotation.walkthrough: 'Papers' looks like sheets to be flattened, but it is the newspapers.
annotation.definitionFit: Two plain senses: ironing or squashing something flat, and the collective name for newspapers and journalists.

entries.clue: Offensive sight I noticed, reportedly (7)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: as it is said, not as it is spelt

blocks.note: 'I saw' said in a British accent, with no R sound

annotation.surface: Someone claims to have spotted something offensive.
annotation.walkthrough: This works in a non-rhotic British accent, where 'sore' and 'saw' sound the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, and the answer's own parts agree: a sight that makes the eye sore.

entries.clue: Diggers in use, sometimes skirting cavities (7)

indicatorNotes.skirting: the answer runs along the words, touching their edges

annotation.surface: Mechanical diggers working round holes in the ground.
annotation.walkthrough: The building-site picture makes 'cavities' holes in the ground; they are the air spaces in the skull.
annotation.definitionFit: Sinuses are the air-filled cavities in the bones of the face.

entries.clue: Tops of trees axed in great American pine forest (5)

indicatorNotes.Tops of: the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of Trees Axed In Great American

annotation.surface: Treetops lopped in a vast American pine forest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tops of trees' looks like foliage and 'axed' like logging; 'Tops of' governs every word after it up to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The taiga is the vast northern coniferous forest.

entries.clue: Can a bribe upset West Indian? (9)

annotation.surface: Wondering whether a bribe might offend someone from the West Indies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as offend; it is the anagram instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Caribbean describes the West Indies and their people.

entries.clue: Groups of actors throw opening of scene (5)

indicatorNotes.opening of: a word's opening is its first letter

annotation.surface: Actors hurling themselves into the opening scene.
annotation.walkthrough: The theatre words hide that 'throw' is simply CAST, sharing a word with the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A cast is the group of actors in a production.

entries.clue: Offer extremely elegant bathroom fitting (5)

indicatorNotes.extremely: take the extremes, the first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of ELEGANT

annotation.surface: A sales pitch for a very stylish bathroom fixture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely elegant' reads as 'very stylish'; it gives ELEGANT's outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A bidet is a low basin fitted in a bathroom.

entries.clue: Guards dropping heads in doorways (7)

indicatorNotes.dropping heads: the head, or first letter, is dropped

annotation.surface: Guards nodding off in doorways.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dropping heads' pictures drowsy sentries; it removes the S at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an entry is a way in, and a doorway is the commonest one.

entries.clue: I involved donors at home (7)

annotation.surface: Someone involving donors in a fundraiser at home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Involved' reads as taking part; it mixes I with DONORS.
annotation.definitionFit: Indoors means inside the house, at home.

entries.clue: Brings up yearly leases (7)

annotation.surface: Raising the subject of annual leases.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brings up' reads as mentioning; here it means raises children, and PARENTS is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To parent a child is to bring it up.

entries.clue: Sways accountants? (7)

annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented word: to tot up is to add, so people who tot are totters, and accountants do that all day.
annotation.definitionFit: To totter is to sway unsteadily; tot-ters are people who tot up.
